In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical indications for CMRM have increased dramatically since 2004 and are now well established and widely adopted for the diagnosis and management of a wide range of cardiac conditions.

CMR is a first line, level 1A imaging modality for the assessment of myocardial infarction, viability, myocardial iron overload and cardiomyopathy, and a level 1B imaging modality for aortic disease, congenital heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, valvular disease and pericardial disease.

CMR is now the first line imaging modality for the assessment of myocardial viability and the assessment of cardiac function in patients with heart failure, and that CMR is also the first line imaging technique for assessing the aortic root in patients with Marfan Syndrome.

the number of Level 1 indications for CMR has increased from 6 to 10 and the total number of indications has increased from 26 to 37.
the indications for CMR have increased in both number and strength of evidence and that the clinical applicability of CMR has increased dramatically in the 16 years since our previous report.
